text:
node-alert-bot: ALERT: PCIe AER + NVLink flaps detected on rack13-node03 (gpu0-gpu3). Correctable ECC spikes x15 in 5m, Xid 79 observed on gpu1, NVLink link down/up 3x. Affected pods: inference-prod-*/replicas=4. Graph: https://metrics.redwood.internal/graphs/alert/1964512345
Maya: seeing throughput drop ~35-45% for large-context batches, queues pile up. Noticed elevated batch lat p50->p95.
Jonah: can you paste dmesg / kernel logs from the node? suspect riser/card or BIOS AER suppression.
Maya: grabbing logs now.
Maya: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus. 
[ 12345.679012] pcieport 0000:64:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[ 12345.679123] nvlink: link 0 status: down -> up (transient)
[ 12350.680000] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU reported an error, resetting etc.
```
Rachel: confirmed the k8s node shows kernel oopses and container restarts. pods on gpu1 restarted 3x in 10m.
Ash: ipmi sensor temps are fine (GPU HOT=62C). No obvious power warnings.
Jonah: run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PCI` and `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` on the node. Also collect `lspci -vvv -s 65:00.0`.
Maya: pasted nvidia-smi output: ```
GPU 1: ECC errors (corrected): 18
PCIe Bus Error: AER type: Multiple Corrected
NVLink errors: 3
```
SRE-Oncall: please cordon/drain node while we triage to avoid noisy neighbor impact. Reassigning load to spare GPUs in eu-west1.
Maya: starting drain: `kubectl drain rack13-node03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300`. Will monitor eviction progress.
Jonah: quick check — are we low on spare capacity in eu-west1? autoscaler shows pool at 82% committed. If drain causes scale-up, startup time ~18-25m.
Rachel: scaling headroom is tight, but we can evict non-critical sandbox pods first. I'll patch podDisruptionBudget for heavy models to prefer eviction elsewhere.
Ash: hardware triage suggestion: reseat riser for slot 2 and run BIOS with AER logging disabled temporarily to see if flaps reduce. But only during maintenance window.
Jonah: don't disable AER globally, we need the logs for RMA. Prefer to repro with node in maintenance and run stress test (cuda-memtest + nvlink stress).
Maya: filing infra ticket and RMA pre-checks. Ticket: INFRA-7248. Marking node for replacement if errors persist after reseat & stress.
Maya: Proposed immediate steps: 1) cordon/drain (in flight) 2) move critical inference traffic to dedicated fallback cluster in us-west (30ms extra latency) 3) run remote stress + log capture 4) schedule local tech to reseat riser and run pci-e loop tests 5) open RMA if still failing.
SRE-Oncall: +1 to plan. Set a 1h check-in. If failures continue after reseat -> RMA and permanent drain.
Rachel: added a temporary routing rule in the controller to avoid rack13 for the next 2h. Push config now.
Jonah: capturing serial console logs and attaching to INFRA-7248. If we see repeated Xid 79 with identical offsets, likely faulty GPU silicon.
Maya: drain completed, pods rescheduled. Throughput recovered ~10% after eviction but we still see variance until replacements spin up.
Ash: FYI: logging `lspci -vvv` shows AER capability set, error status increments on function 65:00. Recommend placing a label `needs-rma=true` on the host after tech checks.
Maya: tagging host and adding notes to ticket. RMA hold flag set.
SRE-Oncall: thanks team. Follow-up actions assigned: Jonah (logs & stress), Ash (hardware reseat), Rachel (traffic reroute), Maya (ticket + RMA). Check-in at 1964512940 (~10m). :thumbsup:
